messages.text: For a Automotive use case involving automotive radar, where would Signaling / Non-signaling Tester fit in the test workflow?

Short answer: in an automotive radar use case, Signaling / Non-signaling Testers such as CMX500/CMW/CMP180 do **not** fit as the radar-target/echo test instrument; automotive radar testing is covered by an automotive radar echo generator such as R&S AREG800A, whose purpose is dynamic artificial object / radar echo generation for FMCW radar up to 3000 m [5][12].  
CMX500 fits **adjacent automotive connectivity testing**, not radar echo testing: it is a one-box network emulation and measurement solution for LTE, 5G NR FR1/FR2, WLAN signaling, TX measurements, fading, BLER, throughput, PER, application tests, IMS/audio and related wireless-device functions [9]. In automotive, CMX500 is directly supported for NG eCall testing on Snapdragon Auto 5G Modem-RF under realistic network conditions, simulating a PSAP and validating voice/data transmission against EN 17240:2024 [11]. So CMX500 belongs in the workflow around telematics/connectivity R&D, RF/application verification, eCall/IMS validation, pre-conformance, desense or non-signaling verification—not in radar echo generation [1][10][11].  
CMP180 fits **production non-signaling RF testing for connectivity**, especially WLAN/cellular/non-cellular RF measurements, not automotive radar: the Wi-Fi 7 workflow maps CMX500 to R&D signaling/interworking testing and CMP180 to production non-signaling RF testing [15]. In production, WLAN RF measurements are executed in non-signaling mode to save time, and CMP180 is positioned for that purpose, supporting technologies including Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz [22].  
For CMW/CMW500, the provided passages only mention it in relation to NGeCall over LTE capability-list coverage alongside CMX500, not as an automotive radar tester or as a fully defined workflow step [3]. Therefore, the supported conclusion is that CMW is also not evidenced here as an automotive radar instrument; at most, it is adjacent to automotive cellular/eCall connectivity testing where separately documented [3].  
【推論】A practical workflow split would be: use AREG800A in the radar-sensor validation bench for target/echo simulation, use CMX500 in R&D and pre-conformance-style connected-vehicle telematics/eCall/cellular/WLAN validation, and use CMP180 in production non-signaling RF checks for connectivity modules [5][10][11][15][22].
